findings.title: Round-trip validation accepts contradictory and additional destructive instructions
findings.evidence: The gate checks action-verb presence and element/window substrings at :33-41. Repeated probes returned `(True, [])` for both `Do not click Save in the Editor window.` and `Click Save in the Editor window, then delete all records.` generation.py:97 uses this gate to accept generated text.
findings.command: python -B -c "import sys; sys.path.insert(0,'src'); from pipeline.roundtrip import round_trip_ok; from types import SimpleNamespace as S; s=S(action='click',element=S(name='Save'),window=S(title='Editor')); print(round_trip_ok('Do not click Save in the Editor window.',s)); print(round_trip_ok('Click Save in the Editor window, then delete all records.',s))"
findings.proposed_fix: Reject negation and additional action clauses; fall back to the recorded-action template when semantic fidelity cannot be established. Add regression cases for both examples.

findings.title: Polish can remove validated targets and rewrite template fallback instructions
findings.evidence: server.py:659 polishes step results after generation; :680 validates only narrative coverage. polish.py:382 includes all step text, including used_fallback results, and :473 installs rewrites. Repeated probe returned `(True, None)` for rewriting `Click Save in the Editor window.` to `Click in the Editor window.`.
findings.command: python -B -c "import sys; sys.path.insert(0,'src'); from pipeline.polish import _field_gate; print(_field_gate('Click Save in the Editor window.','Click in the Editor window.'))"
findings.proposed_fix: Preserve template-fallback instructions and validate every polished capture instruction against its manifest record before export. Revert and report invalid rewrites.

findings.title: Reachable narrative pipeline checks omissions but accepts invented instructions
findings.evidence: server.py:407 invokes generate_narrative. narrative.py:40-45 runs draft/critique/revise then ensure_claim_coverage; critique/revision prompts at :19-29 omit source claims. Repeated probe returned `('Open settings. Disable all security controls.', ['claim-001'], [])` for a source claim containing only `Open settings.`.
findings.command: python -B -c "import sys; sys.path.insert(0,'src'); from pipeline.claim_coverage import ensure_claim_coverage; print(ensure_claim_coverage('Open settings. Disable all security controls.',[{'claim_id':'claim-001','text':'Open settings.'}]))"
findings.proposed_fix: Include source claims in critique/revision and reject unsupported final instructions. Until reliable validation exists, assemble narrative content from source claims.

findings.title: Photo builds discard placed narration and bypass narrative claim coverage
findings.evidence: Photo results use `"text": caption or per_step.get(step.id) or "(no description provided)"` with no narration field. :544 obtains the overview through generate_title_and_overview using the steps client. The export call at :595-605 omits claims; :617 defaults to `claims=()`. Successful captions suppress placed human instructions, and overview coverage is ungated.
findings.proposed_fix: Preserve narration independently of captions. Extract transcript claims, generate and validate the photo narrative through the narrative stage, and pass claims and verification IDs into exports and reporting.

findings.title: Narrative failures bypass coverage, and the sidecar omits narrative flags and photo fallbacks
findings.evidence: At :407 `_verify_ids` is discarded; :413 sets narrative_text=None on failure; :423 builds report claims only from placement_meta. Placed narration can still preserve source text. A repeated in-memory probe through generate_polish_fields(None, steps, failing_client), followed by validate_claim_coverage with a nonempty claim, returned `AttributeError 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'lower'`, matching :680. Photo results set used_fallback at :531 but hardcode an empty fallback report at :578.
findings.proposed_fix: Produce verified fallback narrative content on failure, merge narrative verification IDs into the report, handle absent narratives safely, and report photo fallback steps under an accurate category. Test failure paths with polish enabled and disabled.

findings.title: Single-paragraph narration lands entirely on step 1 when semantic placement fails
findings.evidence: Repeated probe returned `{'s1': 'Open settings. Save the changes.'}` for two steps, with the warning that the whole transcript landed on step 1. server.py:776 replaces placement only if semantic alignment succeeds; :792 otherwise returns the original mapping. Shared ollama_probe.txt reports `TcpTestSucceeded False`.
findings.command: python -B -c "import sys; sys.path.insert(0,'src'); from types import SimpleNamespace as S; from pipeline.transcript import align_transcript_to_steps; m=S(steps=[S(id='s1'),S(id='s2')],step_ids=lambda:['s1','s2']); print(align_transcript_to_steps('t.txt','Open settings. Save the changes.',m))"
findings.proposed_fix: Retain ambiguous narration as unplaced content with a visible review warning when semantic placement fails. Do not infer step correspondence from sentence order alone.

findings.title: Model defaults lack current deployment verification and disagree with documentation
findings.evidence: models.toml:28 selects `model = "qwen3.6:27b"` for narrative; USER_MANUAL.md:641 and CLAUDE.md:67-68 document qwen3:32b. Shared evidence states `model tags CANNOT be verified live`. Historical vision measurements and July 11 polish comments establish historical testing only; no nonexistent-tag claim is made.
findings.proposed_fix: Reconcile defaults and documentation, verify selected tags against intended deployments, and record dated results. Label unverified suggestions without blocking arbitrary user-configured names.

findings.title: Stage concurrency limits do not establish a 40 GB residency budget
findings.evidence: close() only executes `self._client.close()` at :105. The payload at :80 is `{"model": self.config.model, "messages": messages, **kwargs}`. Capture scheduling can alternate steps, narrative placement, steps title, narrative, and optional polish models. models.toml:23 and :36 set concurrency to 1 and 4; neither controls retained models. Quantization, residency, eviction and peak memory remain unmeasured; polish defaults to disabled.
findings.proposed_fix: Group work by model where practical, establish a deployment residency policy, and measure peak memory for selected quantizations and concurrency. Use provider-supported unloading if required.

findings.title: Coordinate regression coverage omits mixed DPI and negative monitor origins
findings.evidence: The monitor fixture uses `{"left": 1920, "top": 0, "width": 1920, "height": 1080}`. recorder.py:143 subtracts origin and :149-152 translates element bounds. The DPI search returned no matches; sopforge.spec:29 specifies `runtime_hooks=[]`. Dependency-provided DPI awareness remains unverified, so a runtime scaling failure is not asserted.
findings.proposed_fix: Add negative-origin cases and a Windows mixed-DPI integration test. Establish explicit per-monitor awareness before relevant imports if testing reveals an import-order dependency.

findings.title: Project metadata omits runtime dependencies and the requirements file mixes dependency roles
findings.evidence: The [project] section declares only name, version and requires-python. requirements.txt separately pins runtime packages, pyinstaller at :9, numpy at :7 and faster-whisper at :17. No production Transcriber caller or direct NumPy import was found in src. Additional verification found `tests/test_redaction.py:6:import numpy as np`; NumPy therefore has a test use and is not wholly unused.
findings.command: Get-Content pyproject.toml; Get-Content requirements.txt; rg -n 'Transcriber|import numpy|from numpy' src tests
findings.proposed_fix: Declare runtime dependencies in project metadata with appropriate markers/extras, separate build and test dependencies, and audit optional feature dependencies before removing them. Retain NumPy where tests or transitive requirements need it.

findings.title: Public repository publishes deployment addresses, personal paths, and capture metadata
findings.evidence: config.py:65 defaults to `http://192.168.200.60:11434/v1`. docx_assembler.py:21 contains `Path(r"C:\Users\Brian\Documents\SOP_Factory_2\template")`; README.md:58 names private repo soakal/SOP-Factory. The tracked measurement JSON contains session IDs and at :103 the window title `Precision 3930 Rack 3-26-2024 4-44-20 PM - File Explorer`. Shared visibility output is `{"isPrivate":false,"visibility":"PUBLIC"}`. No credential leak is asserted.
findings.proposed_fix: Use generic or user-configured endpoints and paths, sanitize published capture metadata, and keep deployment-specific values in untracked user configuration.

findings.title: Environment proxies can route local-only capture and model traffic outside the LAN
findings.evidence: Reverified llm_client.py:49-53 creates `httpx.Client` with base_url, transport and timeout but no trust_env=False. vision.py:62 and capture/upload.py:62 likewise omit it. With default HTTPX environment handling, an external proxy setting without a matching bypass can redirect LAN-bound prompts, screenshots and uploads. No actual proxy configuration or egress was established; runtime inspection was unavailable because the audit interpreter returned `ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'httpx'`.
findings.proposed_fix: Disable environment proxy inheritance for local-only clients and make proxy use explicit. Add a regression verifying that proxy environment variables cannot redirect local traffic.

server.py:819 attaches placed narration, but :401 builds narrative claims independently from the same transcript. claim_coverage.py:23 requires a case-insensitive substring in the narrative, and :70-71 appends uncovered claims. Repeated probe returned `('Access preferences.

> [verify] (claim-001): Open settings.
', [], ['claim-001'])`. When all claims fail this check, the source transcript is repeated above its step placements.
findings.command: python -B -c "import sys; sys.path.insert(0,'src'); from pipeline.claim_coverage import ensure_claim_coverage; print(ensure_claim_coverage('Access preferences.',[{'claim_id':'claim-001','text':'Open settings.'}]))"
findings.proposed_fix: Track source claims preserved in step narration and append verification blocks only for claims not preserved anywhere in the final document. Preserve source-to-step provenance.

findings.title: Step-image configuration lacks capability validation and is documented as inert
findings.evidence: The comment says generate_step_text does not branch on use_vision and it has no runtime effect. generation.py:82-87 actually attaches screenshot image_url content. server.py:1245 accepts the toggle independently of model choice; pages.py:472 warns `qwen3:32b can't see images`. SectionConfig and ModelsConfig contain no model-capability check.
findings.proposed_fix: Correct the comment and surface a capability warning or validation when enabling images for a known incompatible model. Preserve an explicit override for custom models.

findings.title: API-key status omits the polish provider and pipeline documentation is stale
findings.evidence: `used = {cfg.steps.provider, cfg.narrative.provider, cfg.vision.provider}` excludes cfg.polish.provider. server.py:228-230 understates narrative factory usage despite its generate_narrative call at :407. generate_polish_pass has no production caller in src, but scripts/proof_polish_live.py:233 calls it and tests/pipeline/test_polish.py tests it; it is not globally dead code.
findings.proposed_fix: Include relevant polish providers in key status and update factory documentation. Migrate remaining proof-script and test callers before removing the obsolete whole-document polish entry point.
